physicalNotes: Radius 0.23730971 Jupiter radii from Incha et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.523..474I), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract): 16,965.7 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. No mass is measured: Incha et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.523..474I), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract) gives only an upper limit of 5.2 Jupiter masses, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Incha et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.523..474I), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname INCHA_ET_AL__2023): P 13.102 d
sources.shape: Incha et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.523..474I), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname INCHA_ET_AL__2023): a/R* 34.2; Incha et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.523..474I), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname INCHA_ET_AL__2023): inclination 89.25 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Incha et al. 2023 (2023MNRAS.523..474I), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname INCHA_ET_AL__2023): transit mid-time 2458371.8384 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 764 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
